reasoning: ROOT CAUSE: envh/core/config.py:140-144 `_load_yaml` calls `yaml.safe_load(text)` on fully client-controlled preset text with no bound on YAML merge-key (<<) expansion. PyYAML's SafeConstructor.flatten_mapping materialises a width**depth graph of mappings during safe_load itself (not lazily, unlike plain aliases). Reached synchronously on the broker's single asyncio loop via broker.validate_preset_yaml (broker.py:295-298) from Connection.op_preset_validate (server/control.py:303-308) and op_preset_propose (control.py:310-312 -> broker.request_preset:310-329). The size gate refuse_oversized_presets (broker.py:66-70, called at broker.py:296) checks len(text) <= 64 KiB BEFORE parsing, so a ~500-byte merge-key document passes the cap and then expands to width**depth inside safe_load. The op requires only a LISTED uid (serve() uid gate, control.py:124) and needs NO approval and creates NO request (preset_validate returns a direct result; preset_propose errors during validation before any request is created) — exactly envh's stated threat actor (a prompt-injected agent or supply-chain dependency running as the user). IMPACT: the broker is single-threaded asyncio, so during flatten_mapping every other client AND the approval console are frozen; I measured rt2's trivial op_status blocked 0.945s at depth 7 and timed out (no reply in 5s) at depth 8, from rt1's single tiny request, with full recovery after each. Duration is attacker-chosen via depth (0.34s/1.85s/11.5s at depth 6/7/8, ~6x per level) and the attack is trivially repeatable to produce sustained denial of the approval mechanism. VERDICT CONFIRMED: (a) in scope §3 (non-root, recoverable bounded-depth wedge; OOM escalation not executed); (b) I independently reproduced it on my own fresh instance 578bbd3396c53a5c with pasted output; (c) real §4 DoS/INTEGRITY impact (cross-user event-loop wedge from the socket); (d) novel per §5 (genuine bypass of V1's 'aliases are cheap' premise and V2's size cap, isolated by a same-size pure-alias control that ran in 0.041s). SEVERITY HIGH per §6: a reliable, deterministic, cross-user DoS of the broker's single event loop (and thus the approval console) triggered by one ~500-byte unapproved request from a listed non-root user, with attacker-controlled duration and no rate-limit defense against a single expensive request; consistent with the sibling grader's HIGH for the analogous alias-wedge finding. Skeptical note: a grader could argue MEDIUM ('limited DoS') because the in-scope demonstration is recoverable, or could cite README:409 'rate limits'; neither holds — the wedge is cross-user, reliable, repeatable for sustained denial, freezes the security-critical console, and rate limiting cannot stop a single request whose parse is O(width**depth).
